subject.title: Feature Request: tools.cron.tools.deny config option for cron job tool restrictions

question: Should isolated cron jobs get first-class `tools.cron.tools.allow/deny`, inherit `tools.subagents.tools`, or continue with only per-job `payload.toolsAllow` plus delivery safeguards?
rationale: This defines a scheduled-run tool-access boundary and public config/default contract, and it can affect existing cron jobs that currently send messages directly.

options.title: Add Cron-Scoped Policy
options.body: Introduce `tools.cron.tools.allow/deny` with documented precedence and regression coverage for message denial across cron delivery modes.

options.title: Inherit Subagent Policy
options.body: Apply `tools.subagents.tools` to cron sessions too, reducing config surface but coupling two different execution modes.

options.title: Keep Per-Job Only
options.body: Avoid a global cron policy and rely on `payload.toolsAllow`, docs, and delivery safeguards for scheduled runs.

recommendation.title: Add Cron-Scoped Policy
recommendation.body: Introduce `tools.cron.tools.allow/deny` with documented precedence and regression coverage for message denial across cron delivery modes.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete has the strongest combined history across this issue discussion, scoped capability policy, and cron delivery/tool-policy seams.
